newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on soft peso, Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on soft peso, Greenspan.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 75 basis points at 18.25 percent on Wednesday.
Traders said the session was volatile in the wake of greater-than-expected falls in primary rates and hawkish comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Greenspan.
"Rates were bound to react after primary Cetes rates plunged and with Greenspan sending long bond yields up and battering the peso," a dealer said.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 30 basis points at 20.10 percent.
Traders said Mexican markets fell victim to jitters triggered in financial markets across the world by testimony to the U.S. Senate from Alan Greenspan.
Greenspan, speaking just as the money market opened in Mexico, suggested that U.S. interst rates could increase to contain inflationary pressure, if needed.
"A wave of caution froze activity, most dealers preferred to settle deals early and await further developments," another trader said.
"When Banco de Mexico assigned secondary auctions at rates that were not so high, the market calmed down a little and overnight rates eased," he added.
Overnight rates on Cetes had reached a high of 18.85 percent during the session.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts ended 3.9 centavos weaker at 7.8010/7.8040 per dollar.
Yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were up to 6.78 percent, from 6.65 percent in late trade on Tuesday.
Banco de Mexico drained 758 million pesos from the market by holding two auctions.

Bellwether 27-day Cetes rates fell 87 basis points to 18.59 percent at Tuesday night's central bank primary auction. Money market dealers previously surveyed by Reuters had forecast a fall of 60 basis points.
Fixed-income analysts said that a softer peso and higher secondary rates were signs that primary rates had touched bottom for the time being.
"We had been expecting rates to bottom out for a month and now that seems to have happened," a trader said.

Liquidity of 158 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Thursday from prior central bank participation. Traders added that liquidity would increase by 475 million pesos due to an undersupply of paper at the primary auction.
